title: Naidu Seeks Immediate Central Aid as Two Cyclones Leave Losses Above ₹7,000 Crore
excerpt: The Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister briefed Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in Delhi on Tuesday, with preliminary estimates putting combined damage from Cyclones Arnav and Murasu above ₹7,000 crore.
body:
• Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu met Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi on Tuesday and sought immediate Central financial assistance after two consecutive cyclones damaged the state.
  • Preliminary estimates put the combined losses from Cyclones Arnav and Murasu at more than ₹7,000 crore, according to the state government.
  • Cyclone Murasu alone caused damage estimated at ₹2,484.43 crore, including crop losses across 1,43,617 hectares affecting 1,86,063 farmers, the state's report to the Central assessment team said.
  • A third system, Cyclone Akvan, is forecast to make landfall on the Andhra coast on Friday, November 20 — families with relatives in coastal districts should expect relief decisions and fresh storm preparations to run in parallel this week.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has appealed to Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman for immediate financial assistance to his state, which has suffered extensive damage across several sectors, including agriculture, from two consecutive cyclones. Naidu met Sitharaman in New Delhi on Tuesday, November 17, and briefed her on the state's financial situation and the damage caused by the recent cyclones, The Hindu BusinessLine reported.

The Chief Minister explained that Cyclones Arnav and Murasu, which hit the state in quick succession, together caused losses exceeding ₹7,000 crore on preliminary estimates. He briefed the Finance Minister on the precautionary measures the state government took ahead of the cyclones and on the relief and restoration work that followed, and he noted that despite the impact of El Niño, the state had maintained irrigation water supply to several areas through the Pattiseema project to support farmers who were then hit by the storms.

What the damage assessment shows

"The state said it spent ₹37 crore on emergency response and relief measures."

The scale of the loss is set out in the state government's report to the seven-member Central team that toured the affected districts to assess Cyclone Murasu's damage. The team, led by Chittaranjan Das, Joint Secretary in the Union Home Ministry, split into two groups and inspected damaged fields, canals, roads and houses at nearly 60 locations across Bapatla, Palnadu, Eluru and East Godavari districts, IANS reported.

According to that report, Murasu damaged 1,385 km of roads, with breaches at 36 locations and 65 culverts damaged, for losses of ₹888.84 crore. Crops over 1,43,617 hectares suffered damage worth ₹874.97 crore, affecting 1,86,063 farmers, and horticultural crops across 6,756 hectares were damaged to the tune of ₹337.10 crore. A total of 3,859 houses, including 645 huts, were damaged, along with 10,192 11-kV electricity poles, 6,442 LT poles and 1,448 distribution transformers. The state said it spent ₹37 crore on emergency response and relief measures.

Naidu told the Central team that road connectivity, electricity supply and mobile network services were restored within 24 hours of the cyclone, and he asked the team to submit its report to the Centre within 10 days so that assistance could be released without delay. Central teams have since completed their visits, and their reports are expected shortly.

A longer-term ask: cyclone-resilient infrastructure

Beyond immediate relief, Naidu has argued that coastal Andhra Pradesh needs Central support to build more resilient infrastructure as a permanent answer to repeated cyclone damage. He told the Central team that stronger, more resilient infrastructure was essential to minimise losses in a region that faces cyclones frequently.

The Delhi meeting also covered the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub, the release of Purvodaya funds, region-specific development plans, financial support for the Visakhapatnam Economic Region, and the decisions announced at the Visakhapatnam CII Partnership Summit.

What happens next

The immediate decision now sits with the Centre: the amount and timing of assistance will follow the Central team's damage report. For coastal Andhra Pradesh, the timeline is compressed by the weather itself — Cyclone Akvan is expected to cross the coast on Friday, November 20, which means restoration work from Arnav and Murasu will overlap with preparations for a third landfall in a matter of weeks.
